summary: @servicetitan/acquisition-functions ships an alternate-runtime dropper that executes an obfuscated payload at npm install
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts and chmods it executable, then invokes it against a 727 KB sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation with a ~5000-entry constants array and a shuffle routine), and setup.mjs itself uses the same _0xXXXX identifier / wrapper-property obfuscation. Executing a large obfuscated payload under a freshly downloaded alternate runtime at `npm install` places arbitrary attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine while bypassing Node-oriented supply-chain scanning. The declared purpose (MongoDB Atlas Functions helper library) has no legitimate need for the Bun runtime or install-time execution of an opaque bundle. The package is published under the `@servicetitan/` scope with an empty description and a generic README, consistent with brand impersonation of ServiceTitan to gain installer trust.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
